title: Offload browser computation
goal: Keep rendering responsive during CPU work.

prerequisites: WASM/CSR only. Generate FossilWorker with current blazorwebworker template, keep its actual WebWorkerClient and both JS assets, reference it from the standalone FossilDesk app. Use complete offline project/package/import/document files in Markdown; see E03 expansion.

SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105, runtime/packages 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105 and C# 15. No installed wasm-tools workload or native compiler is required for interpreted WASM. AllowUnsafeBlocks and SupportedPlatform browser enable JSExport marshalling. No AOT claim.

A native Worker-capable browser, matching fingerprinted dotnet.js/runtime assets, _content/FossilWorker scripts and permission to load a module worker are required. Use same-origin local assets; CSP must allow the application scripts, worker creation and WebAssembly compilation. No provider, account, credentials or persistence service is required.

The .NET 10.0.402/C#14 comparison restores 10.0.9 WebAssembly/DevServer packages and runs JavaScript CPU work in a native worker. It is not a backported generated client or a .NET 10 applicability route.
constraints: Create only after browser rendering. Retain ownership of the eventual created client and dispose it if the component leaves during startup. Await DisposeAsync for termination; abrupt page termination does not guarantee component disposal.

Invocation timeout abandons pending results; cancellation interrupts the managed JS await. Neither necessarily stops CPU work. Creation timeout terminates; in-flight creation cancellation may lose the reference while the worker still boots. The sample bounds startup without cancelling its managed await and adopts/disposes late results.

RC2 invoke timeout cleanup reads the latest request ID instead of capturing the timed-out call ID. Serialize this sample's calls; do not claim safe concurrent timed-out requests. Explicit worker disposal terminates all its pending calls; it is not graceful/cooperative job cancellation.

Worker .NET memory is separate from the page. JSExport accepts supported primitive/string interop shapes; no DOM or shared DI state. Serialize complex values explicitly. This fixture uses bounded CPU time and a per-worker completion counter; it is not a production scoring algorithm.

Static SSR cannot run browser workers. Interactive Server work belongs to its server; hosted/Auto composition requires explicit client ownership and is not executed here. No background-tab timing, mobile, AOT, GA, deployment, durable-work or speedup claim.
